default_authority.principle: Even involuntary withdrawal of counsel counts as defence delay. An accused's lawyer is an extension of the accused; the terms 'the defence' and 'the accused' are interchangeable in the s. 11(b) framework.

jurisdiction_variants.variance_description: In R v Pastuch (2022 SKCA 109), the Saskatchewan Court of Appeal treated Legal Aid's systemic mishandling of a file as a discrete exceptional circumstance rather than defence delay. This exception has not been adopted outside Saskatchewan but has not been rejected elsewhere.

controlling_authority.principle: Legal Aid's systemic failure to process a file may be treated as a discrete exceptional circumstance rather than defence delay, depending on the facts.

jurisdiction_variants.notes: Pastuch exception is Saskatchewan only. App must capture cause-of-change field (voluntary / involuntary / legal-aid-failure) so Saskatchewan cases with Legal Aid failure can trigger this variant.

notes: Input model must capture: voluntary / involuntary / legal-aid-failure as cause of change. Legal Aid failure in SK triggers Tier 3 via Pastuch variant.
